We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step 1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So in retrosynthesis, we break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the amine). The target has sulfonamide linking a tolyl amine (the first phenyl with methyl) to a sulfonyl attached to second phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthetic step 1: disconnect S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) where Ar is the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) and the amine is the first phenyl with methyl (p-toluidine). So product: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Step 2: The side chain is an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to the second phenyl via a double bond (C=C) then carbonyl amide with an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). This likely comes from Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid. Then coupling to amine to form amide. So retrosynthesis: break amide C-N to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 2: amide formation (carboxylic acid + aniline). So we get unsaturated acid: c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (i.e., phenyl with α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the acid would be /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl.

Step 3: The unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde (the same phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So break the C=C double bond to give aldehyde on that phenyl and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So step 3: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). So we need template IDs for each step.

We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides, broken: maybe sulfonyl chloride? Not in list. But we can search for templates where product is sulfonamide and reactants include sulfonyl chloride and amine. Use search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] maybe also functional_groups_broken? Not needed. Let's try.
